clinician.trajectory_summary: A six-year-old male presented with left leg pain, worsening limp, and inability to ambulate, with pain localized to the mid-anterior left thigh. Initial radiographs of the knee and lower leg were negative. A repeat radiograph of the hip in October 2022 revealed an ill-defined lytic lesion with pseudotrabeculation in the proximal left femoral diaphysis and a lucency in the inferior femoral neck, suggestive of a pathologic fracture (E001). Orthopedic surgery recommended MRI (E004), but specific findings were not documented. A bone biopsy was performed, showing benign-appearing cystic tissue (E005). A permanent pathology report (E007) ultimately diagnosed an aneurysmal bone cyst. Treatment involved open reduction and internal fixation with pins and a plate for stabilization of the pathologic fracture, curettage of the cyst, and filling the cystic space with an injectable inductive graft and crushed cancellous bone. Physical and occupational therapy were initiated for ambulation with a walker upon discharge post-operative day one (E006).
